sentences.text:
This is a complaint under Section 16 (1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'PFA Act') to the effect that on 03.05.2011, the complainant Ranjeet Singh, Food Inspector had taken, by purchasing, a sample of "Snapple Juice Drink"
CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors.

entities.text: Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page No. 4 of 9 (an article of food) for analysis from accused no. 1, where the said food article was stored for sale for human consumption at the time of taking sample.
The sample consisted of 6x473 ml of sealed glass bottles of "Snapple Juice Drink" bearing identical label declaration and main declaration was noted by Food Inspector on Form VI.

The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Kaushal Kishore,
SDM/LHA.
The sample was thereafter, divided in three equal parts.
Each counterpart containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 and Rules, 1955.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the bottles containing the sample.
Thereafter, notice in the form VI was given to accused no. 1 and price for sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 03.05.2011.

Food Inspector completed the remaining formalities and thereafter one counterpart of the sample bearing LHA code no. 32/LHA/32397 in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form-VII and another copy of memo in Form VII in a sealed cover were sent to Public analyst.
The remaining two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of memo in Form VII in a separate sealed packet were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact condition.

2. The sample was analyzed by public analyst and vide his report no. PFA/Enf./1100/2011 dated 30.05.2011, he opined that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of Rule 32(e) of PFA Complainant vs .

on 1 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9544200/
3 Rules, 1955.
However the sample conformed to standard.

It is the case of complainant that accused No. 1 was the Vendor-Cum-Manager of accused no. 3 i.e. M/s Barista Coffee Company at the time of taking the sample and as such he was incharge of the same and responsible for day to day conduct of its business.
Accused no. 6 is the Firm and accused no. 4 and accused no. 5 are its partners and looked after its day to day CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 5 of 9 business and its products were supplied by accused no. 9 which is company of accused no. 7 and 8, who are the persons in-charge of or responsible to the company for conduct of its affairs.

After the conclusion of investigation, entire case file including the statutory documents, Public Analyst's report and Food Inspector's report were sent to the then Director, PFA Govt. of Delhi vide Section 20 of the PFA Act and the Commissioner (Food Safety) accorded consent to same as per Section 97 of Food Safety and Standards Act.
Thereafter, the present complaint had been filed.
3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 05.05.2012.
Accused persons appeared before the court on 01.09.2012 and were admitted to bail.
Copy of complaint and documents were supplied to all the accused persons and matter proceeded for arguments on the point of notice.

In the meantime, separate applications under section 294 Cr.P.C. r/w Section 19(2)
of PFA Act were moved by accused no. 1 to 6.

Vide detailed order dated 06.12.2013 passed by Ld.
Predecessor Court, accused no. 1 to 6 were discharged.

However, accused no. 7 to 9 were served with notice under Section 251 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C') vide order dated 06.06.2016 for offences punishable under Section 5(ii)/7(ii) and Section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. At the trial, prosecution examined only one witness in support of its case.

PW -1 is Sh. Ranjit Singh, FSO who deposed on the lines of the complaint and exhibited the following documents i.e.
Vendor receipt Ex. PW 1/A, purchase bill Ex. PW 1/A-1, Form VI Ex. PW 1/B, Notice under Rule 14-A Ex. PW 1/B-1, Panchnama Ex. PW 1/C, Raid CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 7 of 9 of Ld. Counsel for accused no. 8 that bar coding is sufficient compliance of Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules.

6. Thereafter, proceedings qua accused no. 8 had been quashed by Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 04.09.2020 in Criminal Appeal No. 562/20 and accused no. 8 stood dropped from the array of parties vide order dated 24.11.2020.
7.

Pursuant to aforesaid order of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, it was submitted by Ld. SPP for the complainant that the complainant/department does not wish to lead any further evidence against accused no. 7 and 9 and prosecution evidence may be closed.
Keeping in view the submissions made by Ld. SPP for complainant, PE stood closed on 24.11.2021.

Statement of accused under Section 281 Cr.P.C. r/w Section 313 Cr.P.C. had been dispensed with as no incriminating evidence came against the accused persons in lieu of order of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India dated 04.09.2020.
Since, accused persons did not wish to lead any defence evidence, matter straightway got fixed for final arguments.
8. I have heard the arguments on behalf of both the parties and carefully perused the record.

9. Suffice it to say, vide order dated 04.09.2020 in Criminal Appeal No. 562 of 2020, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India clearly held that relevant information under Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules 1955 with regards to the lot/code/batch identification, to facilitate it being traced to the manufacturer was duly available in the bar code and which could have been decoded by the bar code scanner.
Since, the presence of bar code on the sample in question was not in dispute, proceedings against CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 8 of 9 accused no. 8 who is also one of the directors of accused no. 9 i.e. M/s V&V Beverages Pvt. Ltd. got quashed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

Thus, applying the similar ratio to the facts of the present case, accused no.
7 who is also the director of accused no. 9 i.e. M/s V&V Beverages Pvt. Ltd. as well as accused no.
9(being the company) cannot be punished for violation of Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules under Section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act.
10.
In these circumstances, accused no. 7 namely Deepak Kumar and accused no. 9 M/s V & V Beverages Pvt. Ltd. are acquitted for the offences under Section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act.

Bail bonds already furnished by accused no. 7 on record are extended for a period of 6 months from today for the purpose of Section 437-A Cr.P.C.
ANNOUNCED IN OPEN COURT ON 01.12.2021 (AKASH JAIN) ACMM-01/
